title: Flux concentration by a permeable prolate spheroid (magnetostatics, axisymmetric, analytic)
description:
Axisymmetric (r, z) magnetostatics: a prolate spheroid of relative permeability mu_r (semi-axes a = 1 mm along z, b = 0.1 mm in r, aspect 10) on the axis of a 20 x 40 mm window in a uniform axial field B0 (external_field ring). The needle flux concentrator of Carey et al. 2026 (Eq. 1) in the one shape where that formula is exact; see experiments/Ben_flux for the paper's needle. Automatic mesh (physics rule: base 0.8 mm = the 40 mm height / 50, the spheroid refined to its 0.1 mm radius / 4 = 25 um) plus two mesh axis bands at 0.5 um: r from the axis to 2.5 um, z from 2 um below the upper tip to 60 um above it. Band ends are cell edges, so the staircase tip sits on a cell edge, the tip probe (50.25 um above it) on a z cell centre and r_axis on the first cell's centre. Point refinements would not do: their bands have no fixed ends, and the rescale between the core rectangle's snapped edges moved them by tens of um, leaving the probe in a ~24 um cell. B_z there falls ~1.6 % per um of height (radius of curvature b^2 / a = 10 um), and the 'at' value is the containing cell's; one host SuperLU solve per mu_r. Sweep mu_r = 10 .. 1e5.
Analytic (prolate spheroidal harmonics, focal distance c = sqrt(a^2 - b^2), xi0 = a / c, Q1(xi) = (xi / 2) ln((xi + 1) / (xi - 1)) - 1): the interior field is uniform, B_in / B0 = mu_r / (1 + N (mu_r - 1)) with the demagnetization factor N = (xi0^2 - 1) Q1(xi0) = 0.0203, so the gain saturates at 1 / N = 49.3 once N mu_r >> 1 (the shape, not the permeability, limits the concentration). On the axis outside, B_z / B0 = 1 - (1 - B_in / (mu_r B0)) xi0 Q1'(xi) / Q1(xi0), xi = (z - z_c) / c, Q1'(xi) = (1/2) ln((xi + 1) / (xi - 1)) - xi / (xi^2 - 1); B_z is continuous at the tip and decays to B0 over ~c.
Derived values tab: gain_core (mean B_z over the middle quarter of the spheroid / B0), H_core (mean H_z there), gain_tip (B_z / B0 at a point on the axis 50.25 um above the upper tip). The staircase surface perturbs N, which the gain sees fully when N mu_r >> 1; tolerances 3 %.
Sweep tab: gain_core vs mu_r with the dashed formula and the 1 / N limit (not checked); use a log mu_r axis.
Line profile tab (last sweep value, mu_r = 1e5): B_axis, B_z on the axis from 25 um to 3 mm above the tip.

parameters.name: B0
parameters.description: applied axial flux density in T

parameters.name: size_r
parameters.description: window radius (the dipole field at the ring is ~4e-5 B0)

parameters.name: r_axis
parameters.description: r of the axis probe and line (centre of the first 0.5 um cell)

parameters.name: d_tip
parameters.description: distance of the tip probe point above the upper tip (a cell centre of the 0.5 um z band)

parameters.name: xi_p
parameters.description: spheroidal coordinate of the tip probe point

parameters.name: G_tip
parameters.description: analytic B_z / B0 at the tip probe point
